money-and-cost.cash_card_notes: The local currency is the Guatemala Quetzal (GTQ). You can't import or export the Quetzal. You can only exchange US dollars in Guatemala. Most international hotels and tourist facilities accept credit and debit cards. Ask your bank whether your ATM card will work in Guatemala. Carry cash if you're travelling to rural areas.

visa-preparation.entry_summary: Buy a tourist card at the airport, allowing a visit of up to 90 days. Guatemala is in the CA-4 agreement with El Salvador, Honduras and Nicaragua: the 90 days cover land travel between the four and run from the first entry into any of them.
visa-preparation.fastest_entry: Tourist card bought at the airport (CA-4, up to 90 days).
visa-preparation.before_departure: Carry a valid passport, a return or onward ticket and evidence of enough money. If routing through the US or Canada, meet their entry or transit rules (an eTA for Canada).
visa-preparation.useful_stay: Up to 90 days across the CA-4 countries; extend before expiry at the local immigration office. Non-tourists or longer stays need a visa.

steps.step: Buy the tourist card at the airport on arrival.
Show a valid passport, a return or onward ticket and evidence of enough money.
Count CA-4 days from the first entry into Guatemala, El Salvador, Honduras or Nicaragua; extend at a local immigration office before expiry.
Pay the airport and security tax in cash on departure, and the exit tax if the ticket doesn't include it.
